metaDescription: Five external condensate pumps for dehumidifiers compared by lift height, flow, noise and safety switch wiring, so water leaves the basement for good.
expertTake: The Little Giant VCMA-20ULS is the pick for a basement that must never flood, thanks to its 20 foot shutoff head and a safety switch you can wire into the dehumidifier. The Stropum is the value pick for a plain dehumidifier with a short run. Anyone whose dehumidifier already has a built-in pump or a floor drain beside it can skip this category.
introParagraphs: A condensate pump is a small float-switched water lifter that sits at the end of a dehumidifier drain hose. It collects the trickle from the machine, then pushes it up and out through a narrow tube when the reservoir fills. Used correctly it turns a bucket-emptying chore into a set-and-forget system.

The part buyers overlook is that the pump is the weak link in the whole setup. If the float sticks or the tubing sags, water backs up into the dehumidifier or onto the floor. Lift height, flow rate and a safety switch that cuts the machine are worth more than the brand name on the box.

products.name: Little Giant VCMA-20ULS 80 GPH Condensate Pump
products.description:
Little Giant built this around a vertical float switch and a thermally protected motor, and the design is very nearly a template for the category. When the float rises it starts the pump, and when the level drops it stops again. A thermal cutout protects the motor if the reservoir ever runs dry, which is the failure that kills cheap pumps most often.

The 20 foot shutoff head means water can climb about that high before flow stops, and in practice usable lift is lower than the shutoff figure. Against the smaller VCMA-15UL at 65 GPH, the 20ULS moves more water faster, which matters if a large dehumidifier sends a heavy stream. The included safety switch has signal leads that can be wired to cut the dehumidifier if the pump fails, a feature the cheapest pumps leave out.

Ownership is simple. Clean the reservoir twice a year to keep slime off the float, and use a short run of tubing with a one way check valve so water does not drain back. Mount it level, near the unit, and test the float monthly by pouring in a cup of water. Go with it when a flood would cost real money.
products.bestFor: Finished basements where a backed-up drain would damage floors or belongings.
pros: Thermally protected motor survives dry runs
Safety switch can be wired to shut the unit off
20 ft shutoff head gives real lifting margin
Vertical float design is proven and simple
cons: Larger body than the compact pumps
Pump noise is audible in a quiet room

products.name: Aquastrong 85 GPH 1/38 HP Condensate Pump, 20 ft Lift
products.description:
Aquastrong uses a vertical centrifugal pump with a removable top, and the removable part is the point. A pump that sits in a wet basement for five years will eventually need a bit of cleaning, and being able to lift out the working section is easier than replacing the whole unit. It also accepts both 115 volt and 230 volt supply, which is rare in a pump this size.

Its 85 GPH rating edges the Little Giant 20ULS at 80 GPH, and both claim the same 20 foot lift class. The difference is that the Aquastrong carries the two signal lead wires for a safety switch in the listing, and the lower motor rating of 1/38 HP suggests lighter construction. Treat the lift figure as a limit, not a target, since friction in a long hose cuts delivered height.

In use, run a vertical tube, keep it kink free and avoid sharp elbows. Clean the reservoir and float twice a year, and confirm the safety wire connects to the right terminals on your dehumidifier. Reach for it when your drain route climbs a long way or the supply is 230 volts.
products.bestFor: Basements where the drain line must climb a long way or the supply is 230 volts.
pros: Lift rating in the 20 ft class
Accepts both 115V and 230V supply
Removable top eases cleaning
Safety switch leads supplied
cons: Lighter motor rating than the Little Giant
Longer hoses reduce real delivered lift

products.name: Stropum Automatic Dehumidifier Pump, 16 ft Drain Height

specList.label: Sensing
specList.value: High and low water delay sensor

products.description:
Stropum is a pump designed around household dehumidifiers rather than HVAC drain pans, and the difference shows in its control scheme. A four level height and flow button lets you trade lift for flow, so a short run can run fast and a tall run can climb. Built-in high and low sensors delay start and stop, which reduces the rapid on and off cycling that wears a pump out.

The 16 foot maximum drain height sits below the 20 foot class of the Little Giant, so it fits shorter basements and window wells. The 99 GPH figure is the maximum setting, so the real figure at full lift is lower. Compared with the Asurity at 22 feet, it gives up some height but adds finer control.

Expect to set the level once, test with a jug of water and then leave it alone. Clean the sensors with a soft brush when the reservoir slimes up, and check the outlet check valve each season. Its sweet spot is a tidy dehumidifier setup without wiring in an HVAC safety circuit.
products.bestFor: Household dehumidifiers with a moderate lift to a sink or window well.
pros: Four level height and flow control
Delay sensors reduce rapid cycling
Made around dehumidifier drain flow
Compact body fits beside the unit
cons: Lower lift than the 20 ft class pumps

products.name: Asurity ULTRACP-22 Compact HVAC Condensate Pump, 22 ft Lift
products.description:
The Asurity offers the highest lift rating in the group at 22 feet and a motor built to handle condensate up to 160 degrees Fahrenheit. That high temperature rating matters for HVAC drain pans, but it also shows the motor is built conservatively, which helps reliability in a damp basement. A compact case keeps it tucked beside a dehumidifier or inside a utility closet.

Its lift beats the Little Giant 20ULS by two feet, though neither will deliver the shutoff figure through a long hose. As a general HVAC pump, it lacks the dehumidifier-specific tuning of the Stropum. It handles a heavy stream well but gives you no flow adjustment.

By the third year the pump needs a reservoir clean and a float check, the same as any rival. Use the right tube diameter and a check valve to keep water from flowing back. It suits anyone who wants a tall lift in a small package, or when the same pump may later serve an air conditioner.
products.bestFor: Tall lifts in tight spaces, or a pump that may also serve an HVAC unit.
pros: 22 ft lift rating, the highest in the group
Handles condensate up to 160F
Compact body fits tight closets
Wide use in HVAC trades
cons: Not tuned for dehumidifier duty cycles
Delivered height is less than the rating

products.name: Cleartide Ultra-Quiet 25 dB Condensate Pump, 144 GPH
products.description:
Cleartide chases quiet, and a pump next to a bedroom or home office is where that matters. The 25 dB listing figure is a measured claim, not a certified rating, but the design cues back it up: a larger flow capacity means the motor can run at lower effort for the same water. Three indicator lights show power, running and a fault, which is more feedback than most pumps give.

At 144 GPH it moves nearly twice as much water as the Little Giant 20ULS, which is far more than a household dehumidifier ever produces. That surplus is not wasted: it lets the pump clear its tank quickly and then idle. The tradeoff is that high flow with long lift gets weaker, so confirm the delivered height for your route.

Expect to clean the float and reservoir, and to check the fault indicator after a power cut. Keep the pump on a flat surface so the float is free. It suits a living space where pump noise would be noticed.
products.bestFor: A pump in or next to living space where noise matters.
pros: Very low noise rating for a pump
High flow capacity at 144 GPH
Three indicators for status and faults
Wide input voltage range
cons: Noise figure is a claim, not a certified spec
Lift is not stated as high as rivals

buyingCriteria.explanation: Lift is the vertical distance the pump can push water, and the shutoff figure is the best case with a short hose. The Little Giant VCMA-20ULS lists 20 feet and the Asurity ULTRACP-22 lists 22, but friction in a long hose cuts both. Measure your route, add the horizontal run, and choose a pump with at least 30 percent margin.

A household dehumidifier produces roughly a pint or two per hour, a tiny fraction of any pump's capacity. A bigger number like the Cleartide at 144 GPH does not drain faster; it just clears the reservoir in less time. Choose for lift and safety rather than raw flow.

A good pump has signal leads that cut power to the dehumidifier if the pump fails or the reservoir overflows. The Little Giant and Aquastrong 85 GPH both list this. Wire it through the dehumidifier's control circuit or a plug-in cutout so a stuck float cannot flood the floor.

A pump that starts and stops in a quiet room is more annoying than a continuous hum. Units with delay sensors like the Stropum reduce short cycles, and the Cleartide claims 25 dB. Place the pump away from the bed or behind a cabinet if a quiet room matters.

The most common failure is a pump running dry and burning out. A thermally protected motor, as on the Little Giant 20ULS, cuts out on overheating and resets. Cheaper pumps without protection fail quietly and stop draining until you notice a flooded tray.

Slime builds in any warm, wet reservoir, and a float coated in it sticks. The Aquastrong has a removable top for access, and the Stropum has sensors that need a wipe. Pick a pump you can open and rinse without special tools.

specDecoder.meaning: The maximum height at which flow falls to zero, measured with a very short hose. Real working lift is lower.
specDecoder.watchFor: The Little Giant 20ULS lists 20 ft and the Asurity lists 22 ft, so compare them as limits, not delivery.

specDecoder.meaning: Gallons per hour at a stated lift, usually at low lift. The figure falls as the water climbs higher.
specDecoder.watchFor: The Cleartide's 144 GPH and the Stropum's 99 GPH are both maximums at minimal height.

specDecoder.meaning: A rough index of motor size, quoted in fractions like 1/30 HP. A smaller motor is quieter and draws less power but moves less at lift.
specDecoder.watchFor: The Aquastrong at 1/38 HP and the Little Giant at 1/30 HP differ slightly in motor class.

specDecoder.meaning: A cutout that stops the motor when it overheats and resets when it cools. It guards against dry running.
specDecoder.watchFor: The Little Giant lists a thermally protected motor, so confirm the feature on any alternative.

specDecoder.meaning: Low voltage wires that signal an overflow to the connected equipment. They let the pump shut a dehumidifier off.
specDecoder.watchFor: The Aquastrong lists two signal lead wires, so check how they connect to your dehumidifier.

howWeEvaluated.title: Lift and delivery
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared stated lift and shutoff figures and discounted them for real hose runs. The Asurity at 22 ft and the Little Giant at 20 ft led on paper. The Stropum at 16 ft was judged against a realistic basement route.

howWeEvaluated.title: Failure protection
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked for thermal protection, safety switch leads and sensors that prevent overflow. The Little Giant and Aquastrong include signal leads, and the Stropum adds delay sensing. A pump that can flood a floor with no cutoff ranked lower.

howWeEvaluated.title: Noise and cycling
howWeEvaluated.description: We considered rated noise and whether the pump avoids rapid starts. The Cleartide claims 25 dB and the Stropum delays its starts. Quiet matters most when the pump sits near living space.

howWeEvaluated.title: Fit with household dehumidifiers
howWeEvaluated.description: We checked whether each pump suits the slow trickle from a dehumidifier rather than an HVAC drain pan. The Stropum is built for that duty. HVAC pumps like the Asurity work fine but are not tuned for it.

howWeEvaluated.title: Serviceability
howWeEvaluated.description: We rated how easily the reservoir and float can be cleaned, based on the spec sheet and owner feedback patterns. The Aquastrong's removable top helped it. Compact cases that trap slime lost marks.

cards.label: Dehumidifier-specific
cards.text: The Stropum is built around the slow trickle from a household dehumidifier and adjusts flow and height. It is gentler on cycling. Lift is more modest.

cards.label: HVAC-style
cards.text: The Little Giant, Aquastrong and Asurity are HVAC condensate pumps with high lift and safety leads. They suit a dehumidifier well but are built for heavier duty. Pick these when lift or safety wiring matters.

howToChoose.note: Buy the Stropum for simple household use and an HVAC pump for tall lifts or safety wiring.

rows: Wire the pump to cut the dehumidifier

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: Thermal protection, a safety switch lead and a lift rating at least 30 percent above your climb. Add a check valve at the outlet so water does not drain back into the pump.

cards.label: In this comparison
cards.text: The Little Giant VCMA-20ULS is the basement pick, with a 20 ft head and thermal cutout. The Aquastrong 85 GPH is the alternative if you have a long climb or 230 volt supply.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: A flood would damage finished space. The Little Giant VCMA-20ULS with its protected motor and safety switch is the reliable choice.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: The route is short and the dehumidifier sits over a concrete floor. The Stropum or the Cleartide handle that at a lower tier.

maintenance.why: Slime on the float causes it to stick, which stops the pump or leaves it running. A rinse takes minutes.
Pour in a cup of water and confirm the pump starts and stops. This catches a stuck float before a flood.
Kinks and sagging loops trap water and cause backflow. Replace tubing that has gone stiff or cloudy.
A worn valve lets water drain back into the pump and cycle it constantly. Replace it if it leaks.
A loose signal lead defeats the shutoff. Test by lifting the float with the unit running.

faq.q: Do I need a condensate pump for my dehumidifier?
faq.a: Only if the machine has no built-in pump and the drain is higher than the unit or too far for gravity. A floor drain beside the machine needs only a hose.

faq.q: How high can a condensate pump lift water?
faq.a: Ratings run from about 16 to 22 feet at the shutoff point. Real delivery is lower with a long hose, so keep a safety margin.
Not for a household dehumidifier. It produces far less water than any pump can move, so lift and safety features matter more.

faq.q: Can I use an HVAC pump with a dehumidifier?
faq.a: Yes, they work well and often offer more lift and safety leads. Make sure the inlet fits your hose and the connection is secure.

faq.q: Why does my pump keep cycling?
faq.a: Usually a worn check valve letting water flow back, or a float that is slimed. Clean the reservoir and replace the valve.

faq.q: Is it safe to leave a pump running unattended?
faq.a: With a safety switch wired to cut the dehumidifier and a thermally protected motor, the risk is low. Without them, a failure can cause a flood.
